newsitem.title: GERMANY: Fate of German bourse dealing lies in networks.
newsitem.headline: Fate of German bourse dealing lies in networks.

text.p: The future of bourse trade lies in electronic networks -- which may help pave the way for the arrival of Europe's single currency, a board member of the German bourse operating company said on Friday.

"The dealing structure of the future is a network. We are following this route with the German futures and options market DTB and have it with the cash market through the IBIS (electronic trading system) already," Joerg Franke, a board member of Deutsche Boerse, told Reuters.
"With our new EHS system we will take it a stage further," said Franke, referring to the new electronic trading system for all securities, which will replace IBIS in stages over the next two years.
Franke said that a European-wide share index would help in preparing for the challenges of European currency union.

"The development of a European-wide share index, combined with the development of sector-based indices, would be a good way to prepare for the euro," Franke said, adding that the German bourse was currently addressing the issue.
An upswing in contract volumes over the year put the German bourse in a good position, Franke said.
"Measured by this year's performance, we have seen an increase in contract volumes of over 30 percent, an increase which places us number one among the large European bourses," Franke said.

The German bourse announced a strategic alliance on Friday with the Swiss stock exchange, SWX. The two bourses agreed to set up a Zurich-based joint venture company as the basis for a future strategic alliance in futures and options trading.
Franke said the alliance was part of its strategic plan, which was strongly focused on technology. It would also help with controlling development costs.
"The cooperation with the SWX serves the purpose of reducing costs for technological development," he said.
The German bourse was not only looking to other European bourses and the United States for development, but was also looking to penetrate the Asian market further.
Deutsche Boerse already has a presence in Hongkong, which Franke said he hoped could be expanded.
"We are seeking to further expand cooperation on the technology side with the Hongkong stock exchange. We are also involved in general discussions with the SIMEX index in Singapore," said Franke.
He said that the number of bourses in Europe would be trimmed back in coming years.
"There will be fewer futures and options exchanges in Europe, especially those focused on interest rate products," said Franke.
